editorial.brief: Jensen Huang is the story across three feeds: the AI wire reports his exit from Nvidia, he appears on Polymarket, and he took third place on Wikipedia with 304,348 views. U.S. stocks lost steam on the news, and the wire is already asking who replaces him. Elsewhere, SpaceX caught the Starship to end Flight 15 and led Hacker News with 1,007 points.
editorial.cover_sub: Ramayana: Part 1 drew 581,992 views, ahead of Sean Duffy and well ahead of Jensen Huang, whose departure from Nvidia dominates the rest of today's snapshot.
editorial.wiki_deck: Ramayana: Part 1 led Wikipedia with 581,992 views, 1.3 times the runner-up. No other feed in today's data mentions it, so the margin arrives without an explanation.
editorial.letter_headline: Nvidia loses its chief, and Sunday keeps going
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News watches SpaceX catch a Starship and Lovable leak passport data; Lemmy is cross about tech and dating apps; Bluesky mixes Eurovision, Netanyahu and ProPublica; Mastodon wants cats to breathe fire and praises a riverboat crew.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire follows Nvidia without Jensen Huang and Anthropic's oversubscribed IPO talk, while searchers wanted Arshdeep Singh, England against Australia, Daniel Cormier and a Brazilian novela recap.
editorial.markets_deck: Sport only: Utah against Arizona at 45 percent and Texas Tech against Oklahoma State at 100 each draw $1M, beside a Counter-Strike playoff and Shakhtar's Champions League hopes at 0.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,304,292 players, ahead of Dota 2 at 854,923 and PUBG at 739,272. On Twitch, TheBurntPeanut has 54,930 viewers, Rainbow6 37,036 and a Japanese channel 17,460.

wiki_paras: Ramayana: Part 1 topped Wikipedia's read list with 581,992 views. Sean Duffy followed with 434,101, Jensen Huang with 304,348, the domain .xxx with 222,107, and List of highest-grossing Indian films with 172,992. The lead over second place is 1.3 times, a clear margin but not a rout.

The snapshot offers a hint and no proof. The fifth-place article is a list of the highest-grossing Indian films, which suggests readers were already in that corner of Wikipedia. No other feed names Ramayana: Part 1, so what produced 581,992 views is not recorded in today's data.

Places two to four go to Sean Duffy, Jensen Huang and the .xxx domain, a trio with little in common. Of the three, only Huang turns up elsewhere, on the AI wire and Polymarket, and his is the larger story of the day.
letter_paras: Sunday is a one-story day with a lot of weather around it. Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia reached the AI wire, Polymarket and Wikipedia, three feeds of seventeen, and U.S. stocks lost steam. Everything else, from the Starship catch to a Worlds final, ran on its own track and did not touch it.

In the corners, the USGS logged 25 quakes of M2.5 or above, the largest an M5.5 near Fiji. Cloudflare's top domains start with google.com and amazonaws.com. Product Hunt's leader is called /dev/null, with 539 votes. Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced turns up on both Steam and Wikipedia, and the data keeps its reasons to itself.

Taking every feed in the same minute is a discipline about overlap. A name that shows up in three feeds is shared attention, not a story that migrated from one morning to another. Huang counts today because he was in three places simultaneously, and a staggered collection would have blurred that into trivia.

brief: Jensen Huang is the story across three feeds: the AI wire reports his exit from Nvidia, he appears on Polymarket, and he took third place on Wikipedia with 304,348 views. U.S. stocks lost steam on the news, and the wire is already asking who replaces him. Elsewhere, SpaceX caught the Starship to end Flight 15 and led Hacker News with 1,007 points.
